title: Reevaluating Causal Estimation Methods with Data from a Product Release
abstract: arXiv:2601.11845v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Machine learning methods estimate flexible relationships between confounders, treatments and outcomes, making unconfoundedness assumptions in causal analysis more palatable. How successful are these approaches in recovering ground truth baselines? We analyze new data covering an experimental rollout of a software product feature for one group of users and a voluntary opt-in to the same feature for another similar group. Recovering causal effects from nonrandomized data is feasible--but only with careful modeling choices. We offer best practices for more credible treatment effect estimation in modern, high-dimensional datasets and evaluate which tests provide meaningful signals about the reliability of estimated effects.

translated_title: 基于产品发布数据重新评估因果估计方法
translated_abstract: 机器学习方法能够估计混杂因素、处理变量与结果之间灵活的关系，使得因果分析中的无混杂性假设更容易被接受。这些方法在恢复真实基线方面究竟有多成功？我们分析了新数据，这些数据涵盖了一组用户对某软件产品功能的实验性推出，以及另一组类似用户对该功能的自愿选择使用。从非随机化数据中恢复因果效应是可行的——但前提是必须做出谨慎的建模选择。我们为在现代高维数据集中进行更可信的处理效应估计提供了最佳实践，并评估了哪些检验方法能够为估计效应的可靠性提供有意义的信号。
tldr: 本文利用软件产品功能实验推出与自愿加入的真实发布数据，重新评估机器学习因果估计方法恢复真实效应的能力，并提出了现代高维数据下更可信处理效应估计的最佳实践与可靠性检验方法。
en_tdlr: This paper reevaluates machine learning-based causal estimation methods using real-world product release data combining an experimental rollout and voluntary opt-in, offering best practices and reliability tests for credible treatment effect estimation in modern high-dimensional datasets.
